reason: Reproduced at 20:38Z: PowerShell 'Get-Date -Format u' printed 2026-09-28 23:38:48Z while [DateTime]::UtcNow and bash 'date -u' gave 20:38:48Z (TZ Russian Standard Time, +03:00); the 'u' specifier does not convert to UTC. The action is already met by every scheduled mechanism: the 31 live scratchpad/timer.sh waiters (22:47Z 28 Sep to 00:07Z 30 Sep) compare 'date -u +%s' values; in night_checklist.md G0 uses datetime.now(timezone.utc), G1 parses the UTC poll header, G2, nb_try and the T54 waiter use 'date -u' (T54 carries a Z suffix); lb_poll.py:25, e10_watch_loop.py and ladder_watch.py use tz-aware UTC; the run_*.sh loops use 'date -u'. Finals card v5 step 1 already carries the warning. The remaining risk is an ad-hoc agent turn that stamps a CONTEXT line or does a header-age check through PowerShell. CONTEXT.md has no Get-Date warning, and the checklist PRELUDE does not state the rule. This is a valid ops fact with no score effect and no conflict with R1-R10.
fix: Add one line to the night_checklist.md PRELUDE and one CONTEXT line: 'UTC only from bash date -u, [DateTime]::UtcNow or python datetime.now(timezone.utc); never PowerShell Get-Date -Format u (it prints MSK with a Z suffix)'. Nothing to change in timer.sh, lb_poll.py, the watchers or the guards: all are already correct.
realistic_gain: 0 on LB or private score. It is insurance against a 3-hour clock error in an ad-hoc night or finals step. Such an error could fire G0 or a submit early (on 28 Sep, when all 5 of 5 slots are used) or wrongly mark a fresh poll header as stale. The scripted paths are already safe, so the added protection is small.
